nodes.text: Let $z_1,z_2,\ldots \in [0,1]$ be an infinite sequence, and define the discrepancy\[D_N(I) = \#\{ n\leq N : z_n\in I\} - N\lvert I\rvert.\]Must there exist some interval $I\subseteq [0,1]$ such that\[\limsup_{N\to \infty}\lvert D_N(I)\rvert =\infty?\]

#255 : [Er61] [Er64b] discrepancy The answer is yes, as proved by Schmidt [Sc68] , who later showed [Sc72] that in fact this is true for all but countably many intervals of the shape $[0,x]$. Essentially the best possible result was proved by Tijdeman and Wagner [TiWa80] , who proved that, for almost all intervals of the shape $[0,x)$, we have\[\limsup_{N\to \infty}\frac{\lvert D_N([0,x))\rvert}{\log N}\gg 1.\] Additional thanks to : Cedric Pilatte and Stefan Steinerberger Proof expositions (0) If you would like to contribute an exposition of a proof related to this problem, please message a moderator or leave your exposition as a comment.
